Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a form of G3144; unattested:--without witness.
BiblicalUsage: Once, when Paul tells the men of Lystra that God did not leave Himself unattested: Nevertheless he left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness. The word is without witness, and Paul's point is that God is never that — the rain itself is the testimony.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for unattested carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the denial, that the God who gives rain and fruitful seasons has never left Himself without a witness.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
